optionReasons.saa-med-068:option:0: Step Functions orchestrate workflows — does not ingest millions of events per second.
optionReasons.saa-med-068:option:2: SNS by email is notification — no order per device or streaming throughput.
optionReasons.saa-med-068:option:3: No. SQS each message is consumed UMA times — multiple applications do not read the same flow; and Standard does not preserve order.

finalJustifications: Because Kinesis Data Streams orders by partition key inside the shard and allows several independent consumers in MESMO stream — the exact drawing of the requirement.
Because Kinesis deliver each event to a single consumer at a time, ensuring the exclusivity that preserves order per device.
Because Kinesis record events directly in S3 without consumers, and downstream applications read the files in parallel from there.
Because Kinesis eliminates the need for sorting when processing everything in series in a single shard of high capacity and dedicated.

optionReasons.saa-med-139:option:1: No. SQS Standard message consumed SOME — three systems do not read the same message, and there is no replay.
optionReasons.saa-med-139:option:2: Polling in table DynamoDB is inefficient in thousands of records/second and does not give semantics of stream with checkpoint.
optionReasons.saa-med-139:option:3: The SNS delivery in push and DESCARTA — without retention, impossible to reprocess the last 24 hours.

finalJustifications: Because Kinesis Keeps records (24h a 365 days): each consumer reads independently with his checkpoint, and a new algorithm can give replay of the retained period.
Because Kinesis replicates events to a row SQS dedicated by consumer, isolating the rhythm of each downstream system.
Because Kinesis detects algorithm change and reprocesses data automatically for updated consumer.
Because Kinesis saves data forever by default, allowing replay of any period of the history of the stream.

optionReasons.saa-med-239:option:0: Firehose is a service of ENTREGA — does not replace real-time read consumers of a stream.
optionReasons.saa-med-239:option:1: More Shards Increase Throughput TOTAL, but the 2 MB/s of reading CADA shards continue to be shared among consumers — conflict persists.
optionReasons.saa-med-239:option:3: Backoff reduces pressure, but consumers continue to share the same 2 MB/s — treats the symptom, not the throat.

finalJustifications: Because Enhanced Fan-Out gives every registered consumer 2 MB/s DEDICADOS by shard via push HTTP/2 — the consumers stop competing the shared limit.
Because Enhanced Fan-Out removes all the stream throughput limits, starting to charge for the total volume consumed by reading.
Because Enhanced Fan-Out compresses records during delivery, making consumers fit the shared limit of the shard.
Because Enhanced Fan-Out migrates the slower consumers to Firehose, relieving the dispute by 2 MB/s of shard reading.

optionReasons.saa-med-253:option:1: There is no automatic backup of HDFS for the S3 each 5 minutes — protection is internal replication.
optionReasons.saa-med-253:option:2: Master Node coordinates the cluster — it does NOT store a copy of Core Nodes data.
optionReasons.saa-med-253:option:3: The Auto Scaling replenishes NO, but who prevents the PERDA OF DADOS is the replication of HDFS — o DAG Spark recovers computer, not data blocks from HDFS.

finalJustifications: Because HDFS replicates each block in multiple Core Nodes (factor) 3 by default): if a node falls, the sub-replicated blocks are automatically replicated in the remaining nodes.
Because HDFS record each block simultaneously no S3 and on the local disk, and the copy of the bucket restores the knot that fails in the cluster.
Because Master Node reconstructs the lost data from the Spark execution logs, reprocessing the affected partitions.
Because EMR freezes the cluster by detecting the failure of a Core Node, resuming processing when the node is replaced by AWS.

optionReasons.saa-med-268:option:0: One Lambda by non-scale device for thousands of devices — and consumers of Kinesis read by SHARD, not by device filter.
optionReasons.saa-med-268:option:1: Sort DEPOIS processing does not guarantee order processing — side effects have already occurred out of order.
optionReasons.saa-med-268:option:2: SQS FIFO with Message Group ID would solve ordination, but TROCA the whole architecture — the requirement is to solve NO Kinesis existing, where partition key makes the same role.

finalJustifications: Because using DeviceID as a partition key sends all events from the device to the MESMO shard (guaranteed order), while different shards process devices in parallel.
Because the key partition orders events globally among all the shards, guaranteeing the full sequence of the whole fleet's IoT stream.
Because the partition key creates an exclusive shard for each device, physically isolating the flow of each connected sensor from the fleet.
Because the partition key instructs you to Lambda processing each device in a separate thread, paralleling within the same invocation.

optionReasons.saa-med-270:option:1: Migrating to Serverless is an entire platform swap — and does not organize data by age; you would still want to play 2 years of data.
optionReasons.saa-med-270:option:2: Request Cache Helps Repeated IDENTICAL Queries — Various Log Searches Continue Scanning Giant Index.
optionReasons.saa-med-270:option:3: Multiplying shards of the same huge index increases overhead — the problem is scanning 2 years when only 7 days matter.

finalJustifications: Because ISM with rollover creates indexes by period: recent queries only touch hot indexes; old data go to UltraWarm/cold — performance without delete history.
Because ISM automatically deletes data with more than 7 days, keeping the index dry in the size that the wanted ones use.
Because ISM converts the old indices into tables of Athena, Moving Historical Searches for Consultations SQL on the S3.
Because ISM doubles the clusters' nodes in peak search times, absorbing slowness without touching the index structure.

optionReasons.saa-med-294:option:0: DataBrew is preparing VISUAL data — and RDS does not serve as a metadata catalog of the Athena.
optionReasons.saa-med-294:option:2: A Job Spark TRANSFORMA data — is not the discovery tool; and DynamoDB is not the catalogue of Athena.
optionReasons.saa-med-294:option:3: The Registration Scheme versions schemas of STREAMING (Kafka/Kinesis) — and the Athena does not infer scheme alone to catalog.

finalJustifications: Because Glue Crawler sweeps S3, infers the patterns of CSV/JSON and records the tables in Glue Date Catalog — exactly the catalog that Athena consultation.
Because Crawler converts files to Parquet during scanning, and Catalog records the already optimized version.
Because Data Catalog copies data from S3 for a managed relational bank, where the Athena executes the consultations SQL.
'Cause Crawler runs the longings SQL on behalf of the Athena, returning the results along with the inferred patterns.

optionReasons.saa-med-295:option:0: The EMR Spark spins, but requires sizing and managing clusters — more operational effort than demand.
optionReasons.saa-med-295:option:1: Spark in EC2 self-managed is the MAIOR possible effort: installation, tuning, patching, manual scaling.
optionReasons.saa-med-295:option:3: The Redshift is data warehouse — stored procedures are not ETL Spark serverless on S3.

finalJustifications: Because Glue Spark runs SERVERLESS: without cluster to create or maintain, automatic scale and collection by DPU-time only during the job — the least operational effort.
Because Glue is the only service of AWS type approved to run Spark — EMR executes only Hadoop and Hive in clusters.
Because Glue Keeps a dedicated cluster on 24/7 without additional cost, paid at the monthly fixed rate of the service itself.
Because Glue converts the Spark code to SQL of the Redshift, executing the transformations in the already provided warehouse account.
